<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   • This is a full-stack, containerized web application (“AgentGPT”) for assembling, configuring, and deploying autonomous AI agents in the browser.  
   • It comprises a CLI for bootstrapping, a MySQL database (Planetscale in production), a Python/FastAPI-based backend (“platform”), and a Next.js/TypeScript frontend with server-side logic (tRPC, Next-Auth, Prisma).

2. Analyze the file structure  
   • Top-level “cli/” – Node.js CLI scaffolds environment, database, backend, and frontend via Docker.  
   • “db/” – Dockerfile and SQL for the MySQL database.  
   • “platform/” – FastAPI service (SQLModel/Pydantic ORM, CRUD, API routers, AI-agent orchestration, external-service connectors, tests).  
   • “next/” – Next.js frontend & server code: UI components, pages, API routes (auth, tRPC), Prisma client for DB, internal services modules, localization, styling (Tailwind).  
   • “docker-compose.yml” – Orchestrates “db”, “platform”, and “next” containers.

3. Examine README insights  
   • Tech stack: Next.js + TS, FastAPI template, Next-Auth, Prisma & SQLModel, Tailwind, Zod/Pydantic, Langchain, Planetscale.  
   • CLI sets up environment variables, spins up Dockerized MySQL, FastAPI, and Next.js.

4. Main components and interactions (to represent in the diagram)  
   a. Browser (User)  
      – Renders Next.js pages, communicates via HTTPS/WebSockets to the Next.js server.  
   b. Next.js service (Container)  
      – Serves frontend, SSR, static assets, handles authentication (Next-Auth), hosts tRPC endpoints under `/api/trpc`, and communicates directly with the MySQL database via Prisma for user, organization, template, settings data.  
      – Proxies certain agent-related requests to the FastAPI backend for AI orchestration.  
   c. FastAPI platform service (Container)  
      – Exposes REST/SSE endpoints under `/api/agent/*`, `/api/auth/*`, `/api/memory/*`, etc.  
      – Implements CRUD via SQLModel to the same MySQL database.  
      – Coordinates AI agent workflows (Langchain orchestration, task queue, external LLM calls, tool integrations).  
      – Integrates with external services: OpenAI, Serper, Replicate, AWS S3, Pinecone, Wikipedia, etc.  
   d. MySQL database (Container)  
      – Single shared relational store for both Next.js (Prisma) and FastAPI (SQLModel).  
   e. External services  
      – LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Replicate)  
      – Search APIs (Serper, Wikipedia)  
      – Vector DB (Pinecone)  
      – Object storage (AWS S3)  
      – Third-party OAuth providers

5. Architectural patterns and design principles  
   • Separation of Concerns: CLI for setup, Next.js for UI and auth, FastAPI for AI orchestration.  
   • Shared database layer but distinct ORM stacks (Prisma vs. SQLModel).  
   • Micro-service style: two HTTP services behind Docker Compose.  
   • Event/streaming support in FastAPI for real-time agent updates.  
   • Modular AI tooling: each “tool” is a plugin under `web/api/agent/tools`.

6. Tailoring the diagram to this full-stack application  
   • Draw three main service blocks in Docker: CLI (local), Next.js, FastAPI, and DB.  
   • Show Browser → Next.js (HTTP/S, WebSockets)  
   • Show Next.js ↔ DB (Prisma)  
   • Show Next.js → FastAPI (REST/SSE)  
   • Show FastAPI ↔ DB (SQLModel)  
   • Show FastAPI → External APIs (LLMs, search, storage)  
   • Illustrate Docker network boundaries and environment variables provided by the CLI.

7. Diagram-drawing guidelines  
   • Use distinct shapes/colors:  
     – Blue rectangles for containers (Next.js, FastAPI, MySQL)  
     – Green cylinders for the database  
     – Orange clouds for external services (OpenAI, Pinecone, S3)  
     – Grey box for the CLI  
     – Browser icon for the end-user  
   • Label each component clearly (e.g., “Next.js (Prisma/TS)”)  
   • Draw directional arrows with labels (e.g., “Prisma queries”, “REST call /api/agent”)  
   • Group related modules inside each service: NextAuth, tRPC, Prisma client inside Next.js; CRUD, AI-workflow, tool adapters inside FastAPI.  
   • Optionally annotate ports (Next.js:3000, FastAPI:8000, MySQL:3306).

8. Capture essential elements without overthinking  
   • Identify as many modules as makes sense, but group sub-components under a single service box.  
   • Emphasize both server-side aliasing (tRPC vs. REST) and shared state (DB).  
   • Ensure real-time (stream/SSE) and batch interactions are distinguishable.

With this guidance, sketch a high-level architecture diagram that shows Browser, CLI, three Docker containers, shared DB, and external services, complete with arrows, labels, and color-coded shapes to make the system easy to understand at a glance.
